summary: The thesis proposes a polyhedral source-to-source framework that generates low-volume data movement for affine loop nests on clusters and heterogeneous nodes. It also generates a dynamically scheduled dataflow runtime whose task functions are evaluated per node without building the task graph in memory.
why_read: It covers both halves of compiler-driven distributed execution, communication volume reduction and dataflow scheduling, in one worked system.
main_contribution: Flow-out partitioning, a compile-time partitioning of flow dependences that sends each data partition only to its receivers, together with a compiler-generated dataflow runtime interface.
main_limitation: Minimal volume is claimed only for most dependence patterns, and placement and data tiling are left out of scope.
evaluation_method: Communication volume and execution time on a 32-node InfiniBand cluster, a multi-GPU heterogeneous node and a shared-memory multicore, compared with FO, FOIFI, OMPD, UPC, auto-static and Intel CnC.
